questions.question: What is the most common cause of a palpable breast mass in a male?
questions.detail: Gynecomastia is a benign proliferation of the male ductal tissue.

questions.question: "Nodular" gynecomastia is the most common pattern and is characteristically located:
questions.detail: It appears as a "button" of tissue directly behind the nipple.

questions.question: Which pattern of gynecomastia resembles "female-type" breast tissue and is often seen in long-standing cases?
questions.detail: This occurs when the entire breast becomes dense with fibroglandular tissue.

questions.question: Male breast cancer accounts for approximately what percentage of all breast cancers?
questions.detail: It is rare but should be suspected if a mass is eccentric to the nipple or spiculated.

questions.question: Which genetic mutation is most strongly associated with an increased risk of male breast cancer?
questions.detail: Men with BRCA2 mutations have a significantly higher lifetime risk of breast cancer compared to the general male population.

questions.question: Radiographically, male breast cancer is often distinguished from gynecomastia because it is:
choices: Eccentric to the nipple and often spiculated
questions.detail: Cancer typically does not follow the concentric subareolar distribution of gynecomastia.
